description:
Twelve line drawings, one per token, all in a single palette: thin gold/brass strokes on a near-black blue-tinted ground (~#15171d). No fills, no texture, no second hue anywhere in the collection; the only tonal variation is stroke opacity, which runs from a bright solid ochre down to a ghosted 20-30% wash. Every token is a centred emblem: a bright continuous OUTER CONTAINER (a circle, a hexagon, a square, or a rotated square/diamond) enclosing a denser INNER TANGLE of overlapping polygons, rings, tiny circles and dots. The idiom is sigil / seal / heraldic badge / alchemical diagram. Nothing bleeds off the frame in the neutral row; each emblem sits in the middle 70-80% of a square tile with a generous dark margin all round.

What the twelve have in common: the container-plus-core structure, the single gold hue, the uniform hairline stroke weight, the centring, and a strong tendency to bilateral mirror symmetry. What separates them: (a) the container silhouette - circles on 1203347, 1243682, 1283437, 1475115, 1561509, 1985692; hexagons on 1310661, 1366079, 1446330, 1733538; a square on 1835793; a diamond on 1991107; (b) symmetry - 1243682, 1283437, 1366079, 1446330, 1310661 and 1733538 are cleanly mirrored about a vertical axis, while 1203347, 1475115, 1835793, 1991107 and 1985692 are scattered/asymmetric; (c) density, which swings very wide - 1561509, 1310661 and 1283437 are packed to near-mush, while 1985692 (a small square holding two tiny marks inside a large empty ring) and 1475115 (a pea-sized knot inside three big concentric rings) are almost empty.

Several read as FACES, and I do not think that is accidental. 1243682 has a literal eye - a concentric circle with a pupil dot - at the base of a diamond under a fanned crown of squares. 1283437 reads as an animal cranium or mask with a pendant ring hanging below it like a lock or a lantern; it is the single-token 512px sheet as well. 1561509 reads as a helmeted head with two little circular feet at the bottom. 1366079 reads as a crowned totem figure. The other seven read as abstract seals rather than creatures.

Across the three market states the change is large and obvious, and it is a change of ORDER rather than of colour or subject. Neutral is contained and quiet. STRESS breaks the emblem: elements rotate off-axis, escape the container and hit the frame edge. 1203347's stress frame loses its outer circle entirely and becomes a tumbling drift of squares running out of the top-left corner. 1243682's stress swaps its circle for a diamond and fans the crown so wide it touches both side edges. 1283437's stress inflates until the top ornament crosses the top edge and the shoulders cross both sides, and its circle becomes a shield/hexagon. 1310661 goes the other way: it SHRINKS and tilts, a small tipped hexagon cluster inside a large empty square, with four loose diamonds at the corners. RECOVERY returns close to neutral but is not a copy of it - 1203347 recovery has noticeably larger circles and a looser tangle; 1310661 recovery is denser than its own neutral, with more hexagonal rosettes; 1243682 and 1283437 recover to a slightly lower, tighter version of the neutral emblem. So the arc reads legibly as intact -> ruptured -> repaired-but-marked.

At 120px, what survives is the SILHOUETTE of the container and the coarse density of the core. Circle-vs-hexagon-vs-square-vs-diamond separates the twelve into visible groups; the interior collapses into a fine gold mesh where you can read dense from sparse but not what the shapes are. The face reads survive: 1243682's eye and 1283437's pendant ring are still legible at 120. The weakest at browse size are 1985692, which reads as an almost-empty ring and looks unfinished, and 1475115, which reads as concentric rings with a smudge; and 1733538 and 1446330 become hard to tell apart, both being a hexagon with a small central core. The stress row is unmistakable at 120 - the scattered, edge-clipping frames read as broken from across the sheet - and the recovery row is very close to, but not identical with, the neutral row.

Things that look like faults: frame clipping in stress on 1203347, 1243682 and 1283437; 1561509's two bottom circles reading as accidental feet; 1985692 and 1475115 being so sparse they read as failed rather than quiet; and in the densest neutrals (1561509, 1310661, 1203347) the interior overlaps mushing together even at 256px.
$redaction: One word of this blind description was replaced, meaning preserved: the reviewer wrote "an animal <reserved> or mask" as a simile for what one token resembles, and that noun is a term the repository-wide reserved-term gate refuses because it would publish another project identity ahead of its own announcement. The substitution is "cranium", it is recorded here rather than made silently, it changes no verdict, and the verdict document itself is untouched.
